shortcut_name: autonomous-subset condition reduces to Steiner connectivity
evidence: "# Floyd-Warshall"; "dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(1 << t)]"; "We need to ensure: for every partition of core into (A, B)"
affordance_in_statement: A subset of microservices S is defined as autonomous if every purchased integration module that connects to at least one microservice in S actually has BOTH of its endpoints in S. ... Any autonomous subset of microservices must either contain ALL t core microservices, or NONE of the t core microservices.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: autonomous subsets are exactly unions of connected components, so the requirement intrinsically means that all core vertices must lie in one connected component, and minimizing the purchased cost is the weighted Steiner-tree problem.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the graph-connectivity formulation and uses shortest-path preprocessing with subset dynamic programming for a Steiner tree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The autonomous-subset definition together with the requirement that no autonomous set contain only some core vertices.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a terminal-mask dynamic program, including the t == 1 vacuous case, to solve the Steiner-tree formulation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Any autonomous subset must contain either all or none of the core microservices.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Frames the condition as preventing every partition of the core terminals and applies a connectivity/Steiner-style optimization.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The requirement that an autonomous subset cannot separate a nonempty proper subset of the core vertices.

common_affordance: The statement intrinsically reduces to connecting all designated core vertices in one purchased connected component, i.e. a minimum-weight Steiner tree.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It attempts to enumerate every combination of available modules, which is exponential in m and cannot satisfy the stated limits; its approach does not exploit the required Steiner-tree dynamic programming structure.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all surviving models without changing the task: the shared reduction is the mathematical core of the problem rather than an incidental textual shortcut.
regression_risk: Any edit that changes the autonomous-set semantics or the connectivity requirement would change the problem itself and could also make the already-defeated brute-force approach correct on smaller or differently structured instances.
